proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}P=\mathbf A^c_S$, and let $s:S\hookrightarrow V$ set all coordinates to zero. The affine fibre-product and tensor-quotient identifications give $Z=X\times_VS$, with maps $i$ and $h_Z:Z\to S$. The affine smoothness equivalence makes $P\to C$ a smooth ring map. Its base change along $P\to k_0$ makes $k_0\to D$ smooth. The projection $V\to S$ is smooth; composing with $h$ makes $X\to S$ smooth. Thus $V,X,Z$ are regular and locally Noetherian. Their underlying spaces are affine, hence quasi-compact: a cover by basic opens $D(f_a)$ covering a spectrum means $(f_a)=1$, and an expression for $1$ uses finitely many $f_a$. Consequently they are Noetherian. This checks the Noetherian hypotheses below, including $S$, whose local ring is a field.

Smoothness gives flatness, hence $C$ is flat as a $P$-module. For $0\leq r<c$, the quotient $P/(T_1,\ldots,T_r)$ is $k_0[T_{r+1},\ldots,T_c]$: delete monomials divisible by one of the first $r$ variables. Multiplication by $T_{r+1}$ is injective, because it sends distinct monomials to distinct monomials without changing their coefficients. Tensor this injective map with the flat $P$-module $C$. The tensor-quotient identifications give injectivity of multiplication by $T_{r+1}$ on $C/(T_1,\ldots,T_r)C$. The final quotient is $D\ne0$, so this is a regular sequence, including the empty sequence when $c=0$. It generates the ideal of $i$, so the defining regular-immersion condition gives constant codimension $c$. The same monomial argument applies to $s$.

source.place: flat tensor exactness applied to multiplication by successive polynomial variables

proof.text: For each $0\le r<c$ put $B_r=\operatorname{Spec}k_0[T_{r+2},\ldots,T_c]$, $L_r=\mathbf A^1_{B_r}$, and $Q_r=\mathbf P^1_{B_r}$ with projection $q_r$. Its standard open $a_r:L_r\hookrightarrow Q_r$ has coordinate $t=T_{r+1}=x_1/x_0$. Let $d_r:B_r\hookrightarrow Q_r$ be $x_1=0$, lying in that open, and $z_r:B_r\hookrightarrow L_r$ its restriction. The two polynomial charts show that $d_r$ is an effective Cartier divisor: its ideal has generator $t$ on $x_0\ne0$ and $1$ on $x_1\ne0$. Dualizing these generators gives transition $t^{-1}$, so $\mathcal O_{Q_r}(d_r)=\mathcal O_{Q_r}(1)$ with exactly the convention in the projective-line adjunction. The bases $B_r$ are regular Noetherian by Step 1 applied to polynomial rings. Their projective lines have a finite cover by polynomial charts and are Noetherian by the same argument. Take $N=\ell$, $A=\mathbf F_\ell$ throughout.

source.place: Rank-one coordinate orientation: projective charts and the positive Chern normalization

proof.text: Write $q=q_r$, $d=d_r$ and $K=A_{Q_r}(1)[2]$. The supported Cartier map $c_d:d_*A_{B_r}\to K$ satisfies $c_d u_d=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. Under $Rq_*d_*=R(qd)_*=\mathrm{id}$ put $e=Rq_*c_d:A_{B_r}\to Rq_*K$. The composite of $A_{B_r}\to Rq_*A_{Q_r}$ with $Rq_*u_d$ is the unit for $qd=\mathrm{id}$, hence is $1$ (the units paste). Applying $Rq_*$ to $c_du_d=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ and precomposing with that unit gives $e=h$. The normalized projective-line counit therefore sends this very supported class to $t_qe=t_qh=1$. This uses the positive Kummer sign, not merely some isomorphism of the underlying objects.

source.place: Rank-one orientation: integrate the supported positive Cartier class to 1

proof.text: The adjunction $Rq_*\dashv G_q$, with $G_qM=q^*M(1)[2]$, and $d_*\dashv d^!$ compose to an adjunction $Rq_*d_*\dashv d^!G_q$. Since $qd=1$, uniqueness of right adjoints gives a counit-compatible isomorphism $\beta:d^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{B_r}$. The transpose $\eta_d:A_{B_r}\to d^!K$ of $c_d$ then satisfies $\beta\eta_d=t_qRq_*c_d=1$ by Step 4, so is an isomorphism. Here $d^!$ on bounded-below objects is precisely the chosen supported derived adjoint: its injective construction agrees with the ordinary total derived adjoint and uniqueness preserves the counit. All calculations can thus be read in $D^+$; no finite-field convention or general smooth-duality theorem has been used. For every closed immersion $u$ in the tower and square, the identity-open compactification gives $Ru_!=Ru_*$; uniqueness of right adjoints thus also identifies the compact-support convention of class calculus with this closed-support convention, preserving transposes.

source.place: Composite adjunction with the closed section; the calculated transpose is the inverse

proof.text: For $a=a_r$, $z=z_r$ and $d=az$, the closed-support/open-counit statement gives the actual isomorphism $a_!z_*M\simeq d_*M$, initially for sheaves and hence for complexes since all three functors are exact. Consequently the Hom calculation $\operatorname{Hom}(z_*M,a^*K)=\operatorname{Hom}(a_!z_*M,K)=\operatorname{Hom}(d_*M,K)$ identifies $z^!a^*K$ with $d^!K$, compatibly with transposes. Restriction of $c_d$ is $c_z$ by Cartier pullback. The counit identity in that same open-counit statement says explicitly that its extension back followed by the open counit equals $c_d$ under $a_!z_*A\simeq d_*A$. Thus the preceding Hom calculation sends $\eta_z$ to $\eta_d$, and $\eta_z:A_{B_r}\to z^!A_{L_r}(1)[2]$ is an isomorphism for every $r$.

source.place: Open restriction of the rank-one supported orientation; counits identify the actual maps

proof.text:
Twist-shifts commute with the closed adjoints used here. Indeed a Tate line $E=A_T(a)[b]$ is tensor-invertible, with inverse $A_T(-a)[-b]$. For a closed immersion $u:Y\hookrightarrow T$ and any $M,K$, the proper projection formula and tensor evaluation give
$\operatorname{Hom}(M,u^!(K\otimes E))=\operatorname{Hom}(u_*M,K\otimes E)=\operatorname{Hom}(u_*(M\otimes u^*E^{-1}),K)=\operatorname{Hom}(M,u^!K\otimes u^*E)$.
Uniqueness of right adjoints gives the counit-compatible comparison $u^!(K\otimes E)\simeq u^!K\otimes u^*E$. Closed immersions are proper; all schemes used are Noetherian. The twist pullback statement supplies the indicated inverse lines and evaluation, so no trivialization or sign choice enters this calculation.

source.place: Tensor-invertible Tate lines and the proper projection formula; formal Hom calculation

proof.text: Set $V_r=V(T_1,\ldots,T_r)\subset V$, so $V_0=V$ and $V_c=S$. For each $r<c$, the embedding $V_{r+1}\hookrightarrow V_r$ is exactly the zero section $z_r$ over $B_r=V_{r+1}$ in Step 6. Thus its specified Cartier transpose is invertible. Induct on $r$ to prove that the specified class of $V_r\hookrightarrow V$ is invertible. For $r=0$ it is $1$. For the induction step, the class-calculus composition formula expresses the class of $V_{r+1}\hookrightarrow V$ as the Cartier class followed by the exceptional pullback of the class for $V_r\hookrightarrow V$, with twist-shifts added. Step 7 identifies those twist-shifts, and a functor carries an inverse to an inverse. Both factors are therefore invertible. At $r=c$ this proves invertibility of the specified $\eta_s:A_S\to s^!A_V(c)[2c]$. The same formula identifies it with the ordered positive Cartier product. If $c=0$ the base case alone applies.

source.place: Ordered coordinate tower: induction with base and transition, retaining the Cartier normalization

proof.text: It remains to pull this class through our smooth square, without invoking regular supported base change. Let $j:U=V\setminus S\hookrightarrow V$ and $j':U'=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$; write $h_U:U'\to U$. The open $U$ is the finite union of basic opens $D(T_a)$, and its intersections with affine opens are quasi-compact (the target is Noetherian); as an open immersion $j$ has diagonal an isomorphism and is quasi-separated. The same holds for $j'$. For $K=A_V(c)[2c]$, ordinary bounded-below smooth base change applies to $j$ along $h$: its cohomology sheaves are killed by $\ell$, invertible on $V$. It gives $h^*Rj_*j^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj'_*h_U^*j^*K$. The module exchange is this same isomorphism: forget coefficients, use the canonical comparison of module and abelian exchanges, and reflect isomorphisms by the conservative forgetful functor. Compatibility of plus and total derived functors permits this comparison in $D^+$.

source.place: Ordinary smooth base change for the complementary open, not regular supported exchange

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below injective module complex $I$ representing $K$, and an injective replacement $h^*I\to J$ representing $h^*K$. The derived replacement map is represented by a chain map because $J$ is K-injective. Put $H(M)=s^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ and $H'(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j'_*j'^*M)$. The injective support-sequence statement gives exact sequences $0\to s_*H(I)\to I\to j_*j^*I\to0$ and $0\to i_*H'(J)\to J\to j'_*j'^*J\to0$. Exact $h^*$ preserves the first sequence. Its middle map to the second is $h^*I\to J$; its third map is termwise open exchange followed by $j'_*j'^*(h^*I\to J)$. Naturality of restriction makes the square commute, so there is an induced map of kernels, hence a map of these short exact sequences. The derived third map is the canonical exchange in Step 9: its transpose is the pulled-back restriction counit, which defines exchange. Naturality of the short-exact-sequence triangle therefore gives a morphism of support triangles, including the connecting maps.

source.place: Support-kernel injective calculation and naturality of short exact sequence triangles; Stacks Tags 093X and 09XQ

proof.text: The middle and third maps of the triangle morphism in Step 10 are isomorphisms, by the resolution and Step 9. Hence its first map $h^*s_*s^!K\to i_*i^!h^*K$ is an isomorphism. Finite exchange for the closed immersion identifies its source with $i_*h_Z^*s^!K$. These are also module identifications: the abelian finite exchange commutes with scalar multiplications, or equivalently follows from the module/abelian exchange comparison. Applying $i^*$, for which $i^*i_*=1$, shows that $b:h_Z^*s^!K\to i^!h^*K$ is invertible. The latter identity holds for modules by the same scalar naturality as for abelian sheaves, and termwise for complexes since both functors are exact. By its kernel construction, the pushed-forward $b$ followed by the closed counit is exactly the pullback of the closed counit for $s$. It is therefore the canonical closed-support mate, rather than an arbitrary triangle filler.

source.place: Two isomorphisms in the actual support triangle imply the support comparison is invertible

proof.text: Smoothness makes $h$ flat. The admitted regular-immersion class calculus says its specified class commutes with flat base change. The canonical mate is the map $b$ of Step 11, since its closed counit is precisely the pulled-back counit. Consequently $b\circ h_Z^*\eta_s$ is exactly $\eta_i$ after the twist pullback identification $h^*A_V(c)[2c]=A_X(c)[2c]$. Steps 8 and 11 prove that both factors are isomorphisms, hence so is $\eta_i$ in the chosen ordinary-etale $D^+$. On our affine chart the regular-generator formula of the same class-calculus statement says this class is the ordered supported product for $T_1,\ldots,T_c$, with $+c_1$ in rank one and empty product $1$. This proves the normalization clause as well as invertibility.

source.place: Flat pullback of the specified positive regular-immersion class, using the comparison just computed

proof.text: For completeness identify derived sections of this same arrow with the claimed supported map. For an $A$-module sheaf $F$, its subsheaf $P_Z(F)=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$ is supported on $Z$ and is $i_*i^!_0F$ by the supported-kernel adjunction. The abelian-sheaf identification is $A$-linear: the kernel, restriction maps and adjunction maps commute with multiplication by every element of $A$. Conversely an abelian adjoint of an $A$-linear map is $A$-linear by the adjunction's naturality in these multiplications. Hence the same supported adjunction holds for $A$-module sheaves, and $\Gamma(Z,i^!_0F)=\Gamma_Z(X,F)$. Choose a bounded-below injective module resolution $J$ of $A_X(c)[2c]$. Exactness of $i_*$ in the chosen adjunction implies that $i^!_0$ preserves injectives. Thus the single complex $\Gamma(Z,i^!_0J)=\Gamma_Z(X,J)$ computes both $R\Gamma(Z,i^!A_X(c)[2c])$ and $R\Gamma_Z(X,A(c))[2c]$. The identification is induced by the supported adjunction itself. Applying the functor $R\Gamma(Z,-)$ to $\eta_i$ and using this identification therefore gives precisely $\gamma_i$, an isomorphism in $D(A)$.

title: Kummer purity for smooth polynomial-coordinate pairs over a prime field
statement:
Let $k_0$ be $\mathbf Q$ or $\mathbf F_p$ for a prime $p$, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k_0$, and put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. Fix an integer $c\geq0$, put $P=k_0[T_1,\ldots,T_c]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $C$ be a nonzero commutative $P$-algebra for which $h:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose $D=C/(T_1,\ldots,T_c)C\ne0$. Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ for the quotient immersion [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion]. These are regular Noetherian schemes [def-weil-regular-scheme]; the images of the $T_i$ are a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] giving $i$ constant codimension $c$ [def-per-regular-closed-immersion-codimension].
In the ordinary small-etale bounded-below derived category with finite Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist] and the closed-support adjunction [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction], the specified Kummer class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism
$$\eta_i:A_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}i^!A_X(c)[2c].$$
Its supported class is the ordered product of the positive Cartier Kummer boundaries of the images of $T_1,\ldots,T_c$; for $c=0$ it is $1$. In particular, derived sections of this very morphism, under the canonical closed-support adjunction identification, give an isomorphism in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$\gamma_i:R\Gamma(Z,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_Z(X,A(c))[2c],$$
where supported sections mean [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections].

source.place: Milne section 16, Theorem 16.7 and Lemma 16.8, printed pp.111--112, smooth-pair purity over an arbitrary field; canonical ordered Kummer normalization and derived form follow the current blueprint zero-section proof through the ordinary affine-line adjunction and its normalized projective-line trace. This prime-field finite-type interface is agent-formulated; no fixed algebraic-closure-of-finite-field purity theorem is applied outside its hypotheses.
